response: The type of tibial component used in unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) does affect mechanical alignment. Specifically, patients who received a metal-backed Onlay tibial component had better postoperative mechanical alignment compared to those who received all-polyethylene Inlay prostheses. The thicker overall construct of Onlay prostheses appears to be an important determinant of postoperative alignment, resulting in higher survivorship rates and improved mechanical alignment. Therefore, Onlay prostheses are recommended as the first option when performing medial UKR.
